conclusion.justification: The report concludes that while observational studies show an association between dark chocolate and lower stroke risk, causal evidence from randomized controlled trials is weak and inconclusive. Because it treats the evidence as insufficient to draw a definitive conclusion, the stance is hedged.
conclusion.label: hedged

report:
**Conclusion: The claim is not definitively false, but causal evidence is weak.**

Observational studies and meta-analyses consistently show an *association* between chocolate consumption and lower stroke risk. A meta-analysis of five prospective studies found a relative risk of 0.81 for high versus low chocolate consumption and 0.86 per additional 50 g/week (https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/nutrition/articles/10.3389/fnut.2025.1696220/full). A broader systematic review similarly reported reduced cardiometabolic risk, including stroke, with chocolate consumption (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8470865/). Prospective cohort evidence suggests moderate dark chocolate intake (3–6 servings/week) is associated with lower stroke risk (https://www.mdpi.com/2072-6643/18/4/636).

However, these are observational data, vulnerable to confounding. The strongest causal test—the large COSMOS randomized trial of cocoa flavanol supplementation—found only a "modest, nonsignificant benefit" for cardiovascular events, and authors note large randomized trials "remain inconclusive" (https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s10654-026-01382-6). One double-blind RCT even failed to show any cardiovascular benefit from short-term dark chocolate consumption (https://ajcn.nutrition.org/article/S0002-9165(23)23556-X/fulltext). Reviewers explicitly state that the lack of large-scale, long-term RCTs "prevents definitive conclusions" about dark chocolate reducing clinical cardiovascular events (https://www.mdpi.com/2072-6643/18/4/636).

**Bottom line:** The association is real in observational data, but causation is unproven. Your skepticism is justified—current evidence does not confidently support dark chocolate as a stroke-prevention strategy.
